items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names say what they do (`worker`, `queue`, `errors`). The docstring covers the cancellation and error behaviour, and an inline comment explains the shield/wait loop. Formatting is consistent.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One function of about 55 lines with a nested worker. It rebuilds structured cancellation by hand (`gather` + `except BaseException` + `while True: await asyncio.shield(asyncio.wait(workers))`) where `asyncio.TaskGroup` would do the same job in a few lines.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Checks `max_concurrent < 1` (ValueError), re-raises CancelledError and catches only Exception. But only `errors[0]` is raised: every later task exception is collected and then thrown away. The broad `except BaseException` path is also hand-rolled.

items.name: Failures and degenerate arguments
items.evidence: An empty list returns at once and `max_concurrent < 1` raises ValueError. When a task raises, the running tasks are not cancelled and queued tasks still start; the error only surfaces after everything finishes (`errors.append(exc)` … `raise errors[0]`). It does not hang or leak tasks.

items.name: Required signature and import behaviour
items.name_zh: 签名与导入行为符合要求
items.evidence: `async def run_tasks(tasks: list[Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]], max_concurrent: int) -> None`. Each callable is called only when a worker picks it up. Standard library only, and importing has no side effects.
